sn35.95:1.1: Then venerable Māluṅkyaputta approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side the venerable Māluṅkyaputta said this to the Fortunate One:
sn35.95:1.2: “Please, reverend Sir, may the Fortunate One preach the Dhamma to me in brief, then I, having heard the Fortunate One’s Dhamma, may dwell solitary, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute.”
sn35.95:2.1: “Now what shall we say to the young monks, Māluṅkyaputta,
sn35.95:2.2: if you, who are an old monk, elderly, of great age, far gone, advanced in years, ask for advice in brief?”
sn35.95:3.1: “Although I, reverend Sir, am old, elderly, of great age, far gone, advanced in years,
sn35.95:3.2: let the Fortunate One preach the Dhamma to me in brief, reverend Sir, let the Happy One preach the Dhamma to me in brief, I will surely understand the meaning of what is spoken by the Fortunate One, I will surely be an heir to what is spoken by the Fortunate One.”
sn35.95:4.2: those forms cognizable by the eye, which have not been seen - which formerly have not been seen, (which) you are not seeing, and which you do not expect to see - can there be desire or passion or love relating to them?”
sn35.95:5.1: “Those sounds cognizable by the ear, which have not been heard - which formerly have not been heard, (which) you are not hearing, and which you do not expect to hear - can there be desire or passion or love relating to them?”
sn35.95:6.1: “Those smells cognizable by the nose, which have not been smelt - which formerly have not been smelt, (which) you are not smelling, and which you do not expect to smell - can there be desire or passion or love relating to them?”
sn35.95:7.1: “Those tastes cognizable by the tongue, which have not been tasted - which formerly have not been tasted, (which) you are not tasting, and which you do not expect to taste - can there be desire or passion or love relating to them?”
sn35.95:8.1: “Those tangibles cognizable by the body, which have not been touched - which formerly have not been touched, (which) you are not touching, and which you do not expect to touch - can there be desire or passion or love relating to them?”
sn35.95:9.1: “Those thoughts cognizable by the mind, which have not been cognized - which formerly have not been cognized, (which) you are not cognizing, and which you do not expect to cognize - can there be desire or passion or love relating to them?”
sn35.95:10.2: in regard to things that are seen, heard, sensed, or cognized, in what is seen there must be only what is seen, in what is heard there must be only what is heard, in what is sensed there must be only what is sensed, in what is cognized there must be only what is cognized. And since for you, Māluṅkyaputta, in regard to things that are seen, heard, sensed, or cognized, in what is seen there will be only what is seen, in what is heard there will be only what is heard, in what is sensed there will be only what is sensed, in what is cognized there will be only what is cognized,
sn35.95:10.3: therefore, Māluṅkyaputta, you will not be with that,
sn35.95:10.4: and since, Māluṅkyaputta, you will not be with that,
sn35.95:10.5: therefore, Māluṅkyaputta, you will not be in that,
sn35.95:10.6: and since, Māluṅkyaputta, you will not be in that,
sn35.95:10.7: therefore, Māluṅkyaputta, you will not be here or hereafter or in between the two
sn35.95:10.8: - just this is the end of suffering.”
sn35.95:11.1: “Of this, reverend Sir, that was spoken in brief by the Fortunate One thus do I understand the meaning in detail:
sn35.95:12.1: Having seen a form and forgotten mindfulness,
sn35.95:12.2: Applying the mind to an object held dear,
sn35.95:12.3: He feels (it) with an excited mind,
sn35.95:13.1: So for him increase various feelings that originate with form,
sn35.95:13.3: And by covetousness and by violence is his mind destroyed -
sn35.95:13.5: For one heaping up suffering like this nibbāna is said to be far away.

sn35.95:24.2: having seen a form he is mindful,
sn35.95:24.3: He feels (it) with an unexcited mind,
sn35.95:24.4: and does not persist in indulging it:
sn35.95:25.1: For he who sees a form and experiences the feeling in this way,
sn35.95:25.3: (Corruptions) are destroyed, not heaped up, he thus lives mindfully -
sn35.95:25.5: For one reducing suffering like this nibbāna is said to be near.

sn35.95:36.1: Of this, reverend Sir, that was spoken in brief by the Fortunate One so do I understand the meaning in detail.”
sn35.95:36.2: “Good, good, Māluṅkyaputta, it is good, Māluṅkyaputta,
sn35.95:36.3: of what was spoken in brief by me so do you understand the meaning in detail:
sn35.95:41.1: Of this, Māluṅkyaputta, that was spoken in brief by me so should you understand the meaning in detail.”
sn35.95:42.1: Then venerable Māluṅkyaputta having rejoiced in and been gladdened by the Fortunate One’s speech, having risen from his seat and worshipped the Fortunate One, after circumambulating (him) departed.
sn35.95:42.2: Then venerable Māluṅkyaputta while dwelling solitary, secluded, heedful, ardent, and resolute, after no long time (attained) that good for which young gentlemen rightly go forth from the house to the houseless life, that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life, and dwelt having known, experienced, and attained (it) himself in this very life.
sn35.95:42.3: Destroyed is (re)birth accomplished is the spiritual life done is what ought to be done there is no more of being in this mundane state - this he knew.
sn35.95:42.4: And venerable Māluṅkyaputta became another of the Worthy Ones.
